meaning: a person who can do many different kinds of work
literal_translation: un manitas que sabe hacer de todo
example: My uncle is a jack of all trades: he can fix the car, paint the house and cook.
origin: The origin is uncertain, but it is an old English expression

wrong_meanings.meaning: a musician who plays many instruments
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: The idiom is about many kinds of work in general, not only music

wrong_meanings.meaning: a person who has a lot of money
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: The idiom has nothing to do with money or being rich

wrong_meanings.meaning: a worker who never finishes a job
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: The idiom describes someone who can do many jobs, not someone who fails to finish work

explanation: 'Jack of all trades' describes someone who is skilled at many different kinds of work. It is often used in a friendly tone, sometimes with 'master of none' to suggest they are not an expert in any one thing.
